action: Rakuten Securities customers: be wary of messages or calls posing as the company or its partners, never share passwords or PINs, and watch for the company's notice.
date_note: Date the company says it learned a third party may have accessed its systems; Security NEXT published on 2026-11-18.
exec: Test-environment data held financial details of millions of brokerage customers, so keep real customer data out of test systems.
plain: Rakuten Securities says an outsider may have reached its systems and some customer details, including income and asset information, may have leaked. It reports no leak of passwords or PINs.
summary: Per Security NEXT, Rakuten Securities said it learned on November 16 that a third party may have accessed its systems, blocked the access and fixed the system. It later found data held in a test environment may have leaked on November 11: details of up to about 4.47 million accounts, including income and financial assets, and customer codes and login IDs for up to about 11.25 million accounts. No password or PIN leak or unauthorised trades were found as of November 17. ITmedia NEWS adds that the company said it copied part of its live customer data to a test server for a fixed period to check functions during a system upgrade, calling this an exception approved through internal procedures.
title: Rakuten Securities says test-environment data on up to about 4.47 million accounts may have leaked

validation.note: Security NEXT and ITmedia NEWS (read in full) independently report the company disclosure; ITmedia adds the company explanation that live data was copied to the test server. Company notice itself not retrieved.
